description:
One-shot operator-only repair for `session_ledger__session` rows whose `last_event_at < first_event_at`. Recomputes both bounds from the canonical `MIN(event_at)` / `MAX(event_at)` over each session's `__event` rows.

This verb backfills the rows already inverted from the earlier M6.5 ingestion. The forward fix lives in `repository.py::upsert_session` (single-statement `LEAST/GREATEST` UPDATE); this verb cleans up the historical damage.

Why inversions existed. Pre-fix the importer passed JSONL line order into `last_event_at` (which an out-of-order vendor stream can land BEFORE the persisted `first_event_at`), and `first_event_at` was never updated after INSERT. A later poll that surfaced an earlier event therefore left `last_event_at < first_event_at`. An example of the inverted shape is a session whose `first_event_at` is later than its `last_event_at`.

Flow. The verb wraps the per-row repair in a try/finally pause-resume envelope around the importer-poll cron: (1) `scheduling_service.clear_scheduled_actions_by_tag(tag)` pauses ingest so a concurrent poll can't re-introduce inversion mid-transaction; (2) `repair_inverted_first_last_event_at` iterates inverted sessions, each in its own `transactional()` block, recomputing MIN/MAX from `__event` and writing back; (3) the `finally` block calls `ensure_periodic_poll_schedule(cadence_minutes, tag)` so the cron resumes even when the per-row loop raises. Sessions whose event-side data yields NULL aggregates (no `__event` rows) are LEFT UNTOUCHED and surfaced via WARN — the inversion can't be event-data-derived.

Default `confirm=False` returns a structured dry-run carrying the inverted-row count (and `resume_outcome='skipped'`, since dry-run never pauses). Pass `confirm=true` to actually run the repair.

This verb is `is_discoverable=False` — the model cannot find it via process_search and never proposes it. Operator-only via the operator bridge.
embedding_description: Operator-only ledger repair: rebuild first/last_event_at for __session rows with inverted bounds from the earlier M6.5 ingestion (upsert path's LEAST/GREATEST forward-fix doesn't cover historical damage). Pauses importer-poll cron, recomputes per-session MIN/MAX over __event in per-row transactions, resumes cron in finally. Default dry-run; confirm=true to commit.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Backfill repair outcome. `confirmed=false` is a dry-run; `confirmed=true` ran the per-row recompute. `inverted_count` is the row count at start; `repaired_count` is the row count actually rewritten (lower when some inverted rows had zero __event rows — those leave a WARN log entry and are left in place).
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: After a confirmed repair, re-run list_sessions with `first_event_since_iso` filters that previously returned inversions; confirm zero rows now match `last_event_at < first_event_at`. If `repaired_count < inverted_count`, the gap is sessions with no events — inspect their entries via get_session_timeline to decide whether to soft-delete them or leave the inversion.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Pause-and-repair pass over `__session` rows with inverted first/last event-at bounds; pauses importer-poll cron, recomputes MIN/MAX from `__event`, resumes cron in finally-block
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: LedgerRepositoryError: the underlying state_service rejected one of the per-session UPDATE statements OR the pause/resume scheduling call failed. If scheduling_service was None, the verb fails fast before the repair loop. Possible causes: schema not yet initialized, state_service unavailable, scheduling_service unbound on this profile.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Confirm scheduling_service is bound (per-profile). Confirm schema is initialized via list_sources. The finally-block re-ensures the importer-poll cron even on exception; if the verb itself raised before the pause call, the cron was never paused and is still running. If the dry-run shows surprisingly large inverted counts, inspect a sample via list_sessions before confirming.
